Country.evidence_source: The Chinese version of the RSES has been shown to have adequate internal consistency and good psychometric properties (Tian, 2006). Previous work with Chinese samples has reported strong correlations between self-reported and measured BMI, with greater accuracy among urban populations (e.g., Zhou, Dibley, Cheng, Ouyang, & Yan, 2010).

Assessment of BA.evidence_source: Participants completed the Body Appreciation Scale (Avalos et al., 2005), a 13-item measure of several related components of positive body image (see Appendix).

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: Using participants' self-reported height and weight, we computed BMI as kg/m2.

Correlation between body appreciation an.evidence_source: The text mentions a negative association between PFRS scores and body appreciation from previous studies, but no correlation between BAS and BMI for the present study is provided.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the materials and measures used in the study. It describes the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (PFRS) for actual-ideal weight discrepancy (used only for women), Rosenberg's Self-Esteem Scale (RSES), and how Body Mass Index (BMI) was computed from self-reported height and weight. Demographic data, including sex, age, religion, and marital status, were also collected. The text refers to 'the present study' and 'participants', implying a single study (Study X).
